companion.meaning: The Companion's signal to the addon. The Companion writes its own data addon, a plain addon (not load-on-demand) that sets one global table; the addon reads it at login. If the global is absent, or `linked` isn't true, the Companion isn't linked.

fields.linked: true while the Companion is linked to an account
fields.uploadedUpTo: server time: every record at or before it has been uploaded; absent until the first upload

pruning: Once per login, the addon drops records: with the Companion linked and `uploadedUpTo` set, those at or before `uploadedUpTo`; otherwise those older than 60 days (at or before the login's server time minus 5184001 s). It prunes with recording turned off too.
A Session is one record, timed by its last row (its end, or where a crash cut it off), and is dropped whole. The current Session (the one that login started) is never dropped.
A reader must expect a Session it has already seen to come back longer: with the Companion, a Session still open when uploaded is kept and later read again with more rows.

Mail rows are Ledger rows, pruned as the next line says. `v1.mails` is not pruned by these rules, since a mail still in the mailbox after its row is dropped must not be recorded again: a key goes a day after its expiry (see `rules`), checked at the same login, so it never holds more than about a month of mails.
A Ledger row is one record, timed by its field 2 (its server time), and dropped on its own; a character left with no Ledger rows is dropped from `v1.ledger`.
A route goes with its Session: it is dropped when its Session is.

`v1.characters` is never pruned: it is how a transfer from a character is recognised after that character's Sessions and Ledger rows are dropped. It stays small without pruning: one short row for each of the account's own characters that has read its mailbox, never anyone else's.
rules: The recording is PriceWatchDB.recording, next to PriceWatchDB.settings. Its `count` is how many Sessions this account has started, ever; each format version's records sit under `v<version>`, so version 1's under `v1`.
Once a record kind ships, it never changes without a new version. A new version writes its records under its own key (`v2`) and leaves the older versions' records as they were until they are pruned.
New record kinds can be added within version 1. Readers skip rows whose kind they don't know.

A row is one line. Its fields are separated by tabs, and each starts with a type tag: `s` a string, `n` a number (as Lua's tostring writes it), `t` true, `f` false. An empty field is nil. In a string, a backslash, tab or newline is written `\\`, `\t` or `\n`, so a row never holds a raw tab or newline.

Field 1 of every row is its kind (a string), and field 2 its time: whole seconds since its Session started, so a reader can place a row whose kind it skips. The rest of the fields are positional, as `kinds` lists them.
Times are server time (the client's GetServerTime: Unix seconds, UTC).

`v1.sessions` maps each Session's ID to its rows, joined by newlines, oldest first; a `start` row is always first. The ID is `<start server time>-<count>`, `count` being the Session's number on this account, so it never repeats there and a /reload keeps it.
`v1.current` is the ID of the Session a /reload continues. A login (or a relog after a disconnect) starts a new Session; a /reload continues the current one.
A Session ends at its `end` row, which is always its last. A Session without one (a crash, or a disconnect) is read as ending at its last row.
A `zone` or `instance` row starts a stop, which lasts until the Session's next `zone` or `instance` row, or its end. The rows between belong to that stop, so a dungeon's time is one stop's.
An `afk` row starts a span away from the keyboard and the next `back` row ends it. A span with no `back` ends when its Session does. AFK time is never time played.

A `death` row starts a span dead and the next `alive` row ends it. A span with no `alive` ends when its Session does; on Hardcore the Session's `end` follows the death at logout as usual. Whether time dead counts as time played is the server's decision: the rows only mark the span.

The mails that end an auction (`salePending`, `sale`, `expired`, `cancelled`) and the AH purchases (`bought`) are Ledger rows of the character in whose mailbox they were first seen, timed when they were. Each is recorded once: a mail seen again, at this opening or a later one, in this Session or a later one, adds no row. Their `expiry` is the mail's expiry in server time to the nearest minute, worked out from the client's days left, so it can differ by a minute from the same mail's expiry seen at another time.

`v1.mails` is the addon's memory of the mails it has recorded, so none is recorded twice; readers can ignore it. Each key is one encoded row: the mail's expiry (as in its row), the character's name and realm, the mail's subject and money, then each attachment's item string and count. Only the auction house's mails keep their subject there (one of the client's own); a mail a player wrote never does (see `transfer` and `received` below). Its value is how many such mails were recorded (identical mails, such as two stacks sold in the same second, each count). A mail matches a key whose expiry is up to a minute either way. A key is dropped a day after its expiry, when the mail is surely gone, never with the Ledger's rows: whenever the mailbox is read, and once per login (even with recording off, the mailbox not opened). `v1.mails` is absent once a login leaves it no key.

`v1.ledger` maps each character to its Ledger rows, joined by newlines, oldest first. The key is `<name>-<realm>`: the character's name and realm as its Sessions' `start` rows hold them, joined by a hyphen; a character's name never holds a hyphen, so the key splits at its first one.
Ledger rows aren't in a Session: their field 2 is the server time itself, not seconds since a Session started.

The player's purchases are Ledger rows, each a Lot with a known cost: `bought` from the AH, recorded from the buyer invoice of the mail that brings the item (one path for buyouts and won bids, as both arrive by mail), and `vendorBought` from a merchant, recorded as the player buys it. Each sale to a merchant is a `vendorSold` Ledger row, recorded as the player sells it, so the Lot it uses up is closed. Buying back an item sold to a merchant is a `buyback` row, not a purchase: it reverses that sale. A client that can't record buybacks records no sales either. What a merchant stocks is never recorded.
`v1.routes` maps a Session's ID to its route, one string per Session (see `route`). Only a Session played with the route on has one, so `v1.routes` is absent until then.

A mail with items that isn't from the auction house (`transfer`, `received`; an auction house mail has an invoice, or can't be replied to and has one of the client's auction subjects) is a Ledger row like the mails that end an auction: recorded once, when the character first saw it in its mailbox, its `expiry` worked out the same way. A mail the character sent that came back to it is not recorded. Its `v1.mails` key leaves the subject and money empty (a player's subject is never kept, and money is taken apart from items) and holds each attachment as first seen. Since the player can take some of its items or its money and leave the rest, such a mail matches a key with empty subject and money whose expiry is up to a minute either way and whose attachments include all of the mail's; of several, the one with the fewest attachments.

`v1.characters` is the account's own characters, so a mail from one of them is recognised as a transfer; readers can ignore it. Each key is `<name>-<realm>` as in `v1.ledger`, and its value an encoded row of that character's Region and Ruleset, as its Session's `start` row holds them. A character is remembered when it reads its mailbox during a Session (as it must to send mail). The account's own characters are those in `v1.characters`, in any Session's `start` row, and in `v1.ledger`'s keys. A sender is one of them when its name is the character's on the receiver's realm, or, failing that, on a realm of the receiver's Region and Ruleset, the Ruleset known (Forever's realms report several names for one Ruleset's mega-realm), or when it is `<name>-<realm>` with the realm's spaces and hyphens left out (a connected realm).

start.meaning: A login started the Session: the character, and the Market it trades in.
fields: name (the character's full name, both words: "First Surname"; the first name alone on a client that gives no surname)
class (the client's file name, e.g. WARRIOR)
race (the client's file name, e.g. Scourge)
Region (us, eu, kr, tw, cn or unknown)
Ruleset (normal, pvp, rp, rp-pvp or hardcore)
House (the faction's: alliance or horde, never neutral; nil if the faction is neither)
money (the character's copper on hand, as the client's GetMoney gives it; nil if the client has no GetMoney)
realm ID (the client's GetRealmID, the backend realm, which the realm name may not tell apart; nil if the client has no GetRealmID)

reload.meaning: The interface reloaded (/reload) at this time, and the Session went on.

end.meaning: The player logged out, or switched to another character.

money.meaning: The character's copper on hand changed (the client's PLAYER_MONEY): written only when it differs from the Session's last recorded balance (in its `start`, `reload` or last `money` row), so the client's own PLAYER_MONEY at a login or /reload adds none. With `start`, `reload` and `end`, it lets a Session's gold be rebuilt: quest gold, vendor sales, repairs, flights, training, mail money and outbid refunds show only here. A raw event: what each change was for is worked out on the server, from the loot, purchase, sale and vendor rows around it. Never written without GetMoney.
fields: money (copper on hand after the change)

loot.meaning: The player took one slot of a loot window: an item, or coin. Slots left in the window aren't recorded; quest items are recorded like any other. A raw event: what it adds up to is worked out on the server.
fields: map (the uiMapID the player was on, as C_Map.GetBestMapForUnit gives it, so it can be smaller than its stop's zone, e.g. a cave or a dungeon's floor; nil if the client can't say)
x (the player's position across that map in thousandths, a whole number from 0 at its left edge to 1000 at its right, as in the route; nil unless the route is recorded, and inside an instance)
y (as x, down the map: 0 at its top edge, 1000 at its bottom)

spell (the spell ID of the player's last successful cast before the window opened, e.g. 8613 Skinning, 2575 Mining, 2366 Herb Gathering, 13262 Disenchant; nil if there was none since the last window. A cast goes to one window only, so skinning a looted corpse is told apart from looting it)
item string (the link's `item:…` part, kept whole, so a Variant's suffix is in it; nil for coin)

then three fields per thing the slot was looted from (a corpse, a node or chest, an item; the client's loot sources), as many as there are: its full GUID (so one corpse looted by several players counts once; its first dash-separated field is its kind, e.g. Creature, Vehicle, GameObject or Item, and for a Creature, Vehicle or GameObject its sixth is the NPC or object ID), the quantity looted from it, and for an Item GUID the ID of the item that went in, e.g. disenchanted (an Item GUID doesn't hold it; nil otherwise, or if the client couldn't say). A fishing loot has none

zone.meaning: The player entered a zone, or the Session started or came out of an instance in one. Never repeated for the zone the player is already in, e.g. after a /reload.
fields: map ID (the client's uiMapID of the zone; a cave or other smaller map counts as the zone it is in)

instance.meaning: The player entered an instance (a dungeon, raid or battleground): one stop however many maps it has.
fields: instance ID (the instance's map ID, e.g. 36 for The Deadmines)
instance type (party, raid, pvp, arena or scenario)

afk.meaning: The player was flagged away from keyboard.

death.meaning: The player died. Never the killer: no player's name, ever.
fields: map (the uiMapID the player died on, as a `loot` row's; nil if the client can't say)
x (the player's position across that map in thousandths, as a `loot` row's; nil unless the route is recorded, and inside an instance)

alive.meaning: The player is alive again, not a ghost: back at the spirit healer or the corpse, or resurrected by another player. A release to ghost is not one, and adds no row.

salePending.meaning: A seller's temporary invoice ("Sale Pending"): one of the character's auctions sold, its money not yet delivered. The buyer is never recorded.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
item name (as the invoice gives it)
quantity (nil if the client's invoice has no count)

sale.meaning: A seller's final invoice ("Auction successful"), with the money: an Observed Sale. The buyer is never recorded.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
item name (as the invoice gives it)
quantity (nil if the client's invoice has no count)

expired.meaning: One of the character's auctions expired unsold and its items came back by mail (the client's AUCTION_EXPIRED_MAIL_SUBJECT, on a mail from the auction house: one the client says can't be replied to, and that isn't the player's own mail come back; a player's mail with that subject is `received`). Its deposit is lost.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
item string (the attachment's link from `item:`, without its name)

cancelled.meaning: The character cancelled one of its auctions and its items came back by mail (the client's AUCTION_REMOVED_MAIL_SUBJECT, on a mail from the auction house, as for `expired`). Its deposit is lost.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
item string (the attachment's link from `item:`, without its name)

post.meaning: A Ledger row: the client confirmed an auction the player posted. Each of its stacks is a Listing of the same Item or Variant, at the same prices, for the same duration, in the Market of the House it was posted at. A post the client never confirms isn't recorded.
fields: server time (when the client confirmed the post)
item string (the link's `item:…` part, verbatim, so a Variant keeps its suffix or bonus IDs)
stack count (1 for a commodity post; for an item post, its quantity, each item its own Listing)
bid per stack, in copper (nil: none, as for a commodity)
buyout per stack, in copper (nil or 0: none; for a commodity, its unit price × its quantity)
deposit for the whole post, in copper

House it was posted at, as the addon's tooltip tells it when the client confirms the post: `neutral` in a zone whose auctioneer is a Neutral one (Booty Bay, Gadgetzan, Everlook), else the character's faction's, `alliance` or `horde` (unlike a Session's `start` row, which is never Neutral); nil when the Market couldn't be told

bought.meaning: A Ledger row: an AH purchase, bought out or won with a bid, from the buyer invoice ("Auction won") of the mail that brings the item. The seller is never recorded.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
item string (the attachment's link from `item:`, without its name, so a Variant keeps its suffix or bonus IDs)
price paid, in copper (the invoice's bid: the buyout, or the winning bid)
buyout, in copper (the invoice's; equal to the price paid when bought out)

vendorBought.meaning: A Ledger row: the player bought from a merchant. Recorded as the purchase is made.
fields: item string (the merchant's link from `item:`, without its name)
quantity (units: the merchant sells in sets, and buying 3 sets of 5 is 15)
copper paid (the merchant's price for a set, per unit times the units, to the nearest copper; nil when paid only in items or currencies)
paid in items or currencies (true or false; when true the copper paid, if any, is only part of the cost)

vendorSold.meaning: A Ledger row: the player sold a bag slot's item to a merchant, using the slot (UseContainerItem) while the merchant window was open. Recorded as the sale is made. An item with no sell price can't be sold and records nothing.
fields: item string (the bag slot's link from `item:`, without its name, so a Variant keeps its suffix or bonus IDs)
copper received (the item's sell price × the quantity)

buyback.meaning: A Ledger row: the player bought back an item just sold to a merchant, from its buyback list. Not a purchase: the game reverses the sale, so the units are back in the Lot the sale used up.
fields: item string (the buyback list's link from `item:`, without its name)
copper paid (what the merchant paid for it)

transfer.meaning: A Ledger row: a mail with items from another of the account's own characters (see `v1.characters`). Each item stays the sender's Lot, with its cost, now the receiver's. Its money isn't recorded.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
sender's name (as its Sessions' `start` rows hold it)
then 2 fields per attachment, in slot order: item string (the attachment's link from `item:`, without its name), quantity

received.meaning: A Ledger row: a mail with items from anyone but the account's own characters and the auction house: another player, an NPC (a quest reward), or a character on another WoW account. The sender isn't recorded. Each item is a Lot of unknown cost. Its money isn't recorded.
fields: server time (when the mailbox first showed the mail)
then 2 fields per attachment, in slot order: item string (the attachment's link from `item:`, without its name), quantity

route.meaning: Where the player went in a Session, recorded only while the Companion is linked or the player has turned "Record route" on. About every 10 seconds (and at each loading screen and zone change), if the player has moved, the map and position become one sample. Inside an instance there is no position, so no sample.
encoding: A route is one string of tokens, each separated by one space, oldest first. Every number in it is written in base 36 with the digits 0-9 then a-z (lowercase).

A token starting with `@` names the map the samples after it are on: `@` then the uiMapID, as C_Map.GetBestMapForUnit gives it (as a loot row's map, so it can be smaller than its stop's zone). A route's first token is always one.

Any other token is a sample. Its last four characters are its x and y, two digits each (`00` to `rs`, 0 to 1000): the player's position on the map in thousandths, as a loot row's x and y. The characters before them, at least one, are its time: seconds since the route's previous sample, or since the Session started for its first.

A sample is added only when the map or the position has changed since the previous one, so standing still adds none: a gap between samples is time the player stood still, spent in an instance, or played with the route off.
route.example: `@13w 0colx acsly @13p kdwdw`: map 1436 at 456, 789 as the Session started; 10 s in at 460, 790; then map 1429 at 500, 500, 30 s in.
route.decoded: A case's `expected.routes` gives each Session's route decoded: each sample as [seconds since the Session started, map, x, y].

size.meaning: Not a rule: how big the recording gets, after 60 days of daily four-hour play with the route on. Spec #44 aimed at about 1 MB; that aim was dropped for this estimate (2.3 to 3.8 MB for busy play), and retention without the Companion, not the format, is the lever if files prove too big. Worked out by hand from rows like this fixture's; KB and MB are 1,000 and 1,000,000 bytes.
assumptions: One four-hour Session a day for 60 days, with the route on, and no Companion (so nothing is pruned before 60 days).
SavedVariables writes each string with its newlines escaped, so each row costs its length plus 2 bytes.

A loot row late in a Session, with a position, one corpse and no cast: an item (`sloot\tn7200\tn1436\tn463\tn790\t\tsitem:2589::::::::60:::::\tn2\tsCreature-0-5250-0-12-589-00004F2A3B\tn2\t`) is 98 bytes, a coin slot 79. With 3 slots in 5 an item, about 92 bytes a loot row; 8 fewer without the route. Before the loot row left out what its GUID already holds (a kind and an NPC or object ID per corpse), it was about 106.

Loot: one slot taken every 30 seconds on average (a busy Session of questing and farming, about 1.3 slots a corpse), so 480 a Session. Lighter play scales it down: 240 (one a minute) and 120 are shown too.
The route: at most one sample every 10 seconds, about 6 bytes each, so at most 1,440 a Session (8.6 KB); always moving is the worst case.

The rest of a Session: its start row (111 bytes with a seven-digit balance and a four-digit realm ID), about 18 zone, instance, afk and back rows (about 29 bytes each), 2 reloads (`sreload\tn7200\tn1234567` is 22 bytes, so 24 a row), its end (`send\tn14400\tn59\tn1234567` is 24, so 26) and 2 deaths, each with its `alive` (`sdeath\tn7200\tn1436\tn500\tn250` is 28, so 30; `salive\tn7200` is 12, so 14): about 0.8 KB.

Money: a money row late in a Session (`smoney\tn7200\tn1234567`) is 21 bytes, so 23 a row. One per balance change: each coin slot looted (2 slots in 5, as above, so 192 a Session at 480 slots) and about 60 more a Session (quest rewards, the vendor sales and purchases below, repairs, flights, training, mail money, deposits and outbid refunds), so 252 changes a Session at 480 loot slots, 156 at 240, 108 at 120.

The Ledger: 10 posts, 10 auction mails, 5 vendor purchases and 20 vendor sales (one row a stack sold, buybacks rare) a day, about 70 bytes a row: 45 rows, 3.2 KB a day. `v1.mails`: about 10 keys of about 100 bytes a day, each kept about a month.
estimate: Loot: 480 × 92 bytes = 44 KB a Session, 2.65 MB in 60 days (1.32 MB at 240 slots a Session, 0.66 MB at 120).
The route: at most 8.6 KB a Session, 0.52 MB in 60 days.
Money: 252 × 23 bytes = 5.8 KB a Session, 0.35 MB in 60 days (0.22 MB at 240 loot slots a Session, 0.15 MB at 120).
The rest of the Sessions: 0.05 MB. The Ledger: 0.19 MB. `v1.mails`: 0.03 MB.

In all: about 3.8 MB at 480 loot slots a Session, 2.3 MB at 240, 1.6 MB at 120. About 1 MB holds only at about 20 loot slots a Session or fewer: loot, one raw row per slot with a full GUID, is most of the recording, and the 60 days without the Companion make it big. With the Companion linked, pruning keeps only what it hasn't uploaded yet, so the file stays at a few Sessions.

cases.name: sale, expiry and cancellation mails, each recorded once over three openings on two days
cases.note: The mails are Ledger rows of First Surname-Forever, timed in server time; the Sessions hold only their start and end. Mailbox entries are what the client's GetInboxHeaderInfo (sender, subject, money, days left), GetInboxInvoiceInfo (invoice: type, item name, buyer, bid, buyout, deposit, AH cut, money delay, eta hour, eta minute, count) and GetInboxItemLink/GetInboxItem (items) return, in inbox order. Opening 1 at 1793790600, in Session 1793790000-1. Expired: 1793790600 + 29.99 days (2591136 s) = 1796381736, minute 29939695.6, so 1796381760. Cancelled: + 29.5 days (2548800 s) = 1796339400.
